title: When an Unemployment Insurance Appeals Case Becomes Final
content:
Under **Unemployment Insurance Appeals**, a lower-authority decision becomes final, and the appeal closes, when the Board of Review filing deadline after the decision mailing date passes with no Board appeal, or when a Board appeal naming it is filed; a Board decision becomes final when the court review deadline passes. A withdrawn appeal closes on confirmation, and a dismissed appeal closes when the reopening window passes without a granted reopening. A closed appeal is never reopened; further review is only by appeal to the next level within its deadline.

## Schedule of finality

| Appeal standing at | Becomes final and closes when |
|---|---|
| decided — lower-authority decision | the Board of Review filing deadline after the decision mailing date passes with no Board appeal, or a Board appeal naming it is filed |
| decided — Board of Review decision | the court review deadline after the Board decision is mailed passes |
| withdrawn | the withdrawal is confirmed |
| dismissed | the reopening window passes without a granted reopening |

## After closure

- A closed appeal is never reopened.
- Further review is only by an appeal to the next level — the Board of Review from a lower-authority docket, the circuit court from the Board of Review — within that level's deadline.

*Illustration (hypothetical):* a lower-authority decision is mailed and, within the Board of Review filing deadline, the employer files a Board appeal naming it. The lower-authority appeal closes on that filing; the matter continues as the Board of Review appeal.
